# ramblin.dev

> A small software shop for small, independent projects that lean pro-social — favoring FOSS, transparent development, and business models where the software user is the customer, not the product.

Right now it's solo: Ivan VenOsdel, building software where the user is the customer rather than the product. Default funding is paid subscriptions or licenses plus voluntary support (GitHub Sponsors, Patreon).

"Ramblin'" is meant in the old American sense — a freedom of travel and informal community exchange (Depression-era ramblers, the Guthrie/folk tradition of trading work, songs, and shelter on the road). The site applies that to creative work: a freedom to make what we wish for others, and receive in kind from a community doing the same.

Long-term, if others join: one shop, not a holding company for separate creator-owned businesses. A 5x pay-ratio cap applies to everyone, comparing total compensation (pay + benefits + equity) per hour worked rather than per year, so part-time staff, contractors, and freelancers fall under the same rule. The goal is a comfortable living doing work you love, not getting rich.

## Pages
- [Home](https://ramblin.dev/): Who Ivan is, current projects, and how to get update emails.
- [About](https://ramblin.dev/about/): The name, the long-term plan, the pay-ratio cap, and how to help.

## Projects
- [Rural Hide + Seek](https://ruralhs.ramblin.dev/): An unofficial fan adaptation of *Jet Lag: The Game*'s Hide + Seek for rural areas without dense transit. Auto-generates a map of "vehicle stations" and uses dice rolls to mimic transit pacing.
